title: MalGuard Privacy | Local-first by design
text: MalGuard privacy summary for local scanning, optional network features and diagnostics. Privacy Local-first, with network use disclosed. This page summarizes the current repository privacy policy. The source policy in MalGuard Core remains the authoritative project document. Local analysis Files selected for supported local scanning are analyzed on the user's device unless a feature explicitly states otherwise. Optional network features Some features may check signed updates, retrieve threat-intelligence metadata, or look up a file hash or other non-file metadata against a configured reputation service. File transfer A file itself must not be uploaded to a third-party service without an explicit user action and clear disclosure. Diagnostics: MalGuard is designed to keep error reporting local-first. Users may choose to export or submit diagnostic information when asking for support. Anonymous release metrics: Official download buttons may use GitHub Release assets so GitHub can expose aggregate download counts. Builds that include first-successful-launch counting make one request to a small public GitHub Release beacon and store only a local marker to avoid counting the same installation again. MalGuard does not attach a user, device, advertising, or installation identifier to that request. Anonymous compatibility report: Packaged Windows builds may send one coarse report after the first successful launch containing only the MalGuard version, Windows build, x64/ARM64 architecture, a bucketed CPU-core range, a bucketed RAM range, and system language. The report excludes account names, computer names, hardware serial numbers, network adapter identifiers, precise location, file paths, scan results, and installation identifiers. The server may forward this report as an administrative notification email when configured. title: MalGuard Labs | Gaming security research and guides
text: MalGuard Labs publishes defensive gaming-security research, explainers and safer-download guidance. MalGuard Labs Research the threat behind the download button. Labs focuses on defensive gaming-security research and clear explanations. It does not publish real malware samples or turn research pages into malware distribution. GUIDE What a SHA-256 hash can prove A SHA-256 fingerprint can prove byte-for-byte identity with a known hash. It cannot tell you by itself whether the matched file is safe, malicious or compromised. GUIDE Static vs behavioral analysis Static inspection studies a file without executing it. Behavioral analysis observes what code does inside an isolation boundary. Each catches things the other can miss. GUIDE Why “SAFE” is not a guarantee A security verdict is bounded by available detectors, file coverage, intelligence and runtime evidence. Responsible tools explain uncertainty instead of hiding it. Threat-model scenario A legitimate mod can be repackaged with extra code. This is a defensive scenario, not a claim about a specific real-world incident. A familiar filename, launcher approval, or popular original project does not prove that a downloaded copy is byte-for-byte identical to the trusted release. What changes An attacker can distribute a modified copy while preserving the original name, branding or expected archive structure. The risky part may be only one added component. What helps Compare trusted hashes when available, verify the download source, inspect structure before use, and escalate suspicious or inconclusive files to deeper analysis rather than treating familiarity as proof. Case study pattern When a legitimate mod is repackaged. A copied name and familiar interface do not prove that a download matches the developer's original bytes. This defensive walkthrough explains the trust gap without distributing harmful samples. Read the case study Research principles Defensive, reproducible, bounded. Safe fixtures MalGuard's repository policy requires harmless synthetic fixtures for tests and forbids adding, downloading or executing real malware in development or CI. title: Repackaged Mods: a defensive incident pattern | MalGuard Labs
text: A defensive MalGuard Labs case-study pattern explaining how repackaged game mods can change without obvious visual differences. MalGuard Labs · Case-study pattern A familiar mod can be repackaged without looking different. This is a defensive incident pattern, not a claim about one named mod or one specific victim. The point is to show why source, fingerprint and analysis matter even when the download looks legitimate. The pattern Same name. Different bytes. A player searches for a popular mod and finds a download that uses the expected name, artwork and description. The package can still differ from the original release. A familiar interface is not evidence that the file is identical. 01 Impersonation A copied page, mirror, direct-message attachment or unofficial re-upload imitates the expected source. 02 Repackaging The package is changed while keeping enough legitimate content that it still appears to be the mod the user expected. 03 Trust gap If the player checks only the filename or screenshots, the changed package may look normal. A published cryptographic fingerprint can reveal that the bytes differ. 04 Deeper inspection Static and, where safely available, isolated behavioral analysis can provide additional signals. No single signal is a guarantee. What players can do Prefer the developer's official release channel. Compare SHA-256 when the publisher provides one. Treat mirrors and direct-message attachments as separate trust decisions. Use security analysis before running an unfamiliar package. What a scanner still cannot prove A clean result does not prove harmlessness. A compromised official account can distribute a correctly hosted but unsafe file. Threat-intelligence coverage can lag behind a new campaign. Unsupported formats or missing isolation evidence must remain visible limitations. Fingerprint a file Known limitations

title: Security policy | MalGuard
text: Security policy | MalGuard MALGUARD / PROJECT DOCUMENTS Security policy Read the project policy here, then send a private report to malguard.security@gmail.com. SOURCE · SECURITY.md · 5e9f5db92053b600d8872ce9cb1713816a866a16 MalGuard Security Policy Scope MalGuard is a defensive security project. It is designed to reduce risk when inspecting supported game-related files and packages, not to provide a guarantee that any file is harmless. Security principles Fail closed when required analysis, integrity, provenance, or isolation evidence is unavailable. Never weaken a security control merely to make a test or release pass. Never download or execute real malware in development, tests, or CI. Use harmless synthetic fixtures only. Treat untrusted files, archives, metadata, offsets, paths, and update metadata as attacker-controlled. Bound resource use where supported and reject malformed or ambiguous inputs safely. Keep update, release, and runtime integrity verification cryptographically bound to expected provenance. Keep release-signing private keys out of GitHub Actions and source control. Require reviewed changes and CI validation before merging security-sensitive changes. Isolation MalGuard includes its own isolation-routing foundations, including MicroVM and portable VM backends. Windows Sandbox may be used as an optional backend on compatible hosts, but it is not a requirement for the MalGuard VM path. No backend may be treated as release-grade merely because a simulated or contract test passed. Host/backend-specific execution evidence must be truthful, and missing evidence must remain fail closed. Release integrity Release candidates are bound to source provenance and package integrity. Public Windows distribution must follow the project's code-signing policy and must not substitute an unsigned or unverified build for a signed release. Reporting vulnerabilities Please report suspected vulnerabilities privately to the maintainers before public disclosure. Include the affected commit/version, reproduction steps using harmless fixtures, expected behavior, and observed behavior. Do not attach real malware. After the repository is public, use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting feature when it is available for this repository. Send a report Project resources

title: Core privacy policy | MalGuard
text: Core privacy policy | MalGuard MALGUARD / PROJECT DOCUMENTS Core privacy policy SOURCE · PRIVACY.md · 5e9f5db92053b600d8872ce9cb1713816a866a16 MalGuard Privacy Policy MalGuard is designed to keep supported file analysis local by default. Local analysis Files selected for local scanning are analyzed on the user's device unless the user explicitly chooses a feature that states otherwise. Network features Some optional features may contact configured services for purposes such as: checking for signed software updates; retrieving threat-intelligence metadata; looking up a file hash or other non-file metadata against a configured reputation service. A file itself must not be uploaded to a third-party service without an explicit user action and clear disclosure. Diagnostics MalGuard's error-reporting design is local-first. Diagnostic information is not automatically published by this repository. Users may choose to export or submit diagnostics when asking for support. Anonymous release metrics Official Windows download buttons may use GitHub Release assets so GitHub can expose aggregate download counts. Packaged Windows builds may make one request after the first successful launch to a small, static GitHub Release beacon asset. MalGuard does not attach a user, device, advertising, or installation identifier to this request, and no scanned file or scan result is included. A local marker stored alongside MalGuard settings prevents the same installation from intentionally sending the beacon again. GitHub may receive standard network metadata, such as the source IP address, as part of serving the public asset under GitHub's own service policies. Users can disable the MalGuard first-launch request by setting MALGUARD_DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_INSTALL_COUNT=1 . Anonymous compatibility report Packaged Windows builds may send one coarse compatibility report after the first successful launch. The report contains only the MalGuard version, Windows build, x64/ARM64 architecture, a bucketed CPU-core range, a bucketed RAM range, and the system language. The report does not include an account name, computer name, hardware serial number, network adapter identifier, precise location, file path, scan result, or installation identifier. MalGuard stores only a local marker so the same installation does not intentionally send the report again. The server may forward the report as an administrative notification email when the notification service is configured. Users can disable this report by setting MALGUARD_DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_COMPATIBILITY_REPORT=1 . Changes If a future release introduces new data collection, telemetry, or external transfer behavior, this policy and the user-facing disclosure must be updated before that behavior is enabled in a public release. title: Code signing | MalGuard
text: Code signing | MalGuard MALGUARD / PROJECT DOCUMENTS Code signing SOURCE · CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md · 5e9f5db92053b600d8872ce9cb1713816a866a16 Code signing policy Current status MalGuard has submitted an application for free open-source code signing through SignPath Foundation. The application is pending review. The project must not claim that a release is signed by SignPath Foundation until the application has been accepted and the actual artifact has passed signature verification. Target OSS signing provider, pending acceptance: SignPath.io / SignPath Foundation. After acceptance, release and download pages will include the required attribution: "Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation." Source and build provenance Release artifacts must originate from the canonical MalGuard/malguard-core repository. Public release candidates must be built from reviewed, merged source. CI actions and build dependencies remain pinned and fail closed according to repository policy. Artifacts are re-opened and integrity-verified after packaging. Source commit/provenance binding must match the expected release source. The current Windows workflow creates unsigned release candidates. By explicit maintainer decision, an installer may be published as an Unsigned Preview only when the release page clearly states that Authenticode is absent and publishes the matching SHA-256 and exact source commit. An unsigned preview must never be described as signed, trusted, production-signed, or equivalent to a future Authenticode release. SignPath integration boundary SignPath configuration identifiers and access tokens are not guessed or pre-created by this repository. After SignPath Foundation accepts the project, integration must use the organization/project/policy/artifact identifiers supplied by SignPath. Any SignPath API access token must be stored only as an Actions secret or provider-managed credential and must never be committed, printed, copied into release artifacts, or exposed in logs. The SignPath GitHub Action, if enabled after acceptance, must be pinned to an immutable full commit SHA and its output must pass the repository's Authenticode verification before it can become a public release. Key handling MalGuard release-signing private keys must never be committed to the repository. Offline release-signing private keys must never be placed in GitHub Actions. Any external signing provider must protect its signing key outside this repository. SignPath-managed Authenticode signing does not replace MalGuard's independent offline Ed25519 release-metadata trust boundary. Approval Every public signing request requires manual approval after CI and integrity verification succeed. Current project roles: Committer: repository owner @MalGuard Reviewer: repository owner @MalGuard Signing approver: repository owner @MalGuard As the maintainer team grows, these roles should be separated across trusted maintainers where practical. text: Contribute to MalGuard, an MIT-licensed open-source defensive game-mod security project. Explore beginner issues, Windows tests, documentation and security review. MALGUARD / PROJECT DOCUMENTS Contributing SOURCE · CONTRIBUTING.md · Live project source Contributing to MalGuard MalGuard accepts defensive-security contributions through reviewed pull requests. We welcome genuine, independent developers who want to improve documentation, accessibility, harmless synthetic regression tests, and transparent security guidance. No previous involvement with MalGuard is required. Engineering contribution areas We are looking for thoughtful contributors, not inflated star counts or promotional posts. These are areas where well-scoped pull requests can help. They are contribution interests, not paid job vacancies . Windows / systems: review file provenance, signatures, archive parsing, and clear limitations in security reports. Testing / quality: write reproducible tests with harmless synthetic fixtures; improve regression coverage without disabling safety checks. Web / accessibility: improve performance, mobile layout, keyboard accessibility, and honest product documentation. Technical writing: document Windows contributor setup, focused tests, and transparent result interpretation. Start by reviewing the public source repository , research guides , and current help-wanted issues . For a first contribution, propose a small change and submit a pull request. Maintainers review the change before merge; contributors do not need write or administrator access. We may separately discuss longer-term collaboration when there is a strong mutual fit, but there is no promised role, compensation, equity or project success. Do not send identity documents or sensitive personal data in a public issue. Start with a small, real task Improve the Windows contributor quickstart Document how to run one focused test Clarify unsigned Windows preview verification Improve sanitized bug report guidance Read the contributor quickstart before opening a pull request. All proposed contributions are reviewed and no issue guarantees acceptance, payment, or code-signing approval. Safety requirements Do not commit, upload, download, or execute real malware. Use harmless synthetic fixtures for security tests. Do not add secrets, API tokens, private keys, certificates, PFX files, credentials, or personal data. Do not weaken fail-closed behavior to make a test pass. Do not introduce hidden network access, telemetry, installers, or update behavior. Do not bypass release provenance, integrity, update, or code-signing controls. Development workflow Create a branch from the current main . Make the smallest reviewable change. Add or update tests for security-sensitive behavior. Run node tests/run-all.js and relevant platform tests. Open a pull request. Require review and green CI before merge. Security-sensitive build, workflow, installer, updater, isolation, and signing changes require especially careful review. Maintainer security Maintainers must use multi-factor authentication for repository access. MALGUARD / GTA MOD SECURITY برنامه بررسی امنیت مادهای جی‌تی‌ای ۵ | مالگارد و GTA Guard اگر دنبال برنامه‌ای برای بررسی فایل‌های ماد GTA 5 هستید، این راهنما کاربرد واقعی GTA Guard، محدودیت‌ها و وضعیت انتشار آن را توضیح می‌دهد. معرفی GTA Guard محدودیت‌های امنیتی پاسخ‌های مستند دربارهٔ مالگارد و GTA Guard مالگارد (MalGuard) چیست؟ مالگارد یک پروژهٔ امنیت بازی است که محصول GTA Guard و راهنماهای بررسی ریسک فایل را معرفی می‌کند. هدف پروژه کمک به تصمیم‌گیری بر اساس شواهد و نشان‌دادن محدودیت‌های تحلیل است. چه برنامه‌ای برای محافظت و بررسی مادهای GTA 5 وجود دارد؟ GTA Guard محصول مالگارد برای بررسی ایستای فایل‌ها و بسته‌های پشتیبانی‌شدهٔ ماد جی‌تی‌ای ۵ در ویندوز ۱۰ و ۱۱ نسخهٔ ۶۴ بیتی است. اسکن ایستا به اجرای کد فایل نیاز ندارد. دانلود عمومی نصب‌کننده بدون رمز از صفحهٔ رسمی دانلود در دسترس است. آیا GTA Guard بی‌خطر بودن همهٔ مادها را تضمین می‌کند؟ خیر. فایل‌های رمزگذاری‌شده، قالب‌های پشتیبانی‌نشده و شواهد ناقص می‌توانند ارزیابی را نامطمئن کنند. نتیجهٔ نامشخص به معنای بی‌خطر بودن نیست؛ منبع دریافت و هویت فایل را هم بررسی کنید. آیا دموی سایت مالگارد ماد واقعی را اسکن می‌کند؟ خیر. پیش‌نمایش وب فقط از نمونه‌های ساختگی استفاده می‌کند و فایل واقعی کاربر را نمی‌خواند، آپلود نمی‌کند یا اجرا نمی‌کند. برنامهٔ ویندوز و دموی مرورگر دو بخش متفاوت‌اند. به جای ادعای «بهترین»، شواهد را بررسی کنید. برای GTA Guard هنوز آمار مستقل دقت روی مجموعه‌ای نماینده از فایل‌های دنیای واقعی منتشر نشده است. محدودیت‌های هر برنامه، پشتیبانی از قالب فایل، منبع دریافت و وضعیت واقعی انتشار را معیار انتخاب قرار دهید. معرفی GTA Guard مستندات فنی مخزن کد پروژه

title: How to Check a GTA 5 Mod Before Downloading | MalGuard Labs
text: Evidence-based safety checklist for GTA 5 mod downloads: trustworthy source, integrity, file types, unsigned installers, static analysis and uncertainty. MalGuard Labs / Guide How to check a GTA 5 mod before trusting it A familiar mod name is not a security guarantee. This defensive checklist helps you investigate a download without executing an unknown file. Published 17 October 2026 . Practical checks Six questions worth asking 01 Where did it come from? Start with the developer's documented distribution channel. Search-result ads, mirrors, shortened links, and unsolicited messages are not proof of authenticity. A familiar-looking domain can also be impersonated. 02 Does the download match an official release? Where a developer publishes a SHA-256 checksum or cryptographically verifiable signature, compare it with the file you obtained. A matching hash supports byte-for-byte identity only when the reference itself is trustworthy. It does not certify that the original file is harmless. 03 What file types are really inside? Inspect an archive's structure, extensions, file signatures and unexpected executables or scripts without launching them. A name such as “readme” or a familiar mod filename does not prove the file's actual format. The format may be unsupported or malformed. 04 Does installation require unusual privileges? Treat unexpected requests for administrator access, security-setting changes or unrelated installers as reasons for further investigation. Do not disable security tools merely to make a mod run. 05 What did the scanner actually inspect? Read the analysis coverage: archive parsing, static signatures, suspicious imports, hashes and unsupported sections. A quiet scanner output can reflect limited visibility as easily as a low-risk file. 06 What remains unknown? If the origin is uncertain, the archive is opaque, or the tool returns an inconclusive verdict, do not treat the file as verified safe. Prefer a trusted copy or avoid using the file. Further reading Technical sources and product limits For robust file type validation and defense in depth, see the OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet . Microsoft's SmartScreen documentation explains why unsigned and unfamiliar installers can trigger warnings. MalGuard's own Trust Center lists the project's limitations. This guide is general security education. It is not a lab test of any particular GTA mod and does not declare any specific download safe. Read scanner verdict guide All MalGuard Labs guides

title: SAFE, SUSPICIOUS and INCONCLUSIVE: Scan Results Explained | MalGuard Labs
text: How to interpret MalGuard-style scanning verdicts, evidence coverage, uncertainty, false positives and why clean static results never guarantee a safe mod. MalGuard Labs / Explainer What can a malware scan result really tell you? A verdict summarizes available evidence. It does not turn an unknown file into a promise of safety. Published 17 October 2026 . Interpreting results Four labels, four different meanings The core documentation describes these verdict categories. Their exact criteria depend on the supported analyzer and version. SAFE No detected concern within the available scope The inspected evidence did not meet the tool's criteria for a warning. This does not mean the file is guaranteed harmless, complete, trusted or independently certified. SUSPICIOUS Signals that warrant caution Some patterns justify further review, but a suspicious result alone is not proof of malicious intent. False positives are possible, especially with unusual or unfamiliar software. MALICIOUS Evidence supports a malicious classification A malicious result is a strong warning about the inspected file. The report should show the evidence and supported detection path rather than presenting a label with no explanation. INCONCLUSIVE Not enough reliable evidence Unsupported formats, incomplete reads, limits, failed checks or unavailable required analysis can leave the answer unresolved. Inconclusive is not a synonym for safe. Quality of evidence Read the coverage before reading the color. Meaningful analysis reports distinguish the real file type, supported structures, parsers that completed, checks that were skipped, warnings that were found and boundaries that could not be verified. A green badge with missing evidence would be misleading. Static analysis inspects bytes and structure without running the file. Behavioral analysis observes execution in an isolated environment. Neither has universal coverage, and a product should never silently present a simulated demonstration as a live safety verdict. Honest limitations Why no honest scanner offers 100% protection Attackers can change packaging and behavior, detection intelligence is incomplete, and parsers have finite budgets. False negatives and false positives can occur. Without a public, representative benchmark and disclosed methodology, numerical detection claims should not be invented. Readers can check MalGuard's documented security approach and its unverified or missing evidence on the project's security evidence page . title: Windows Code Signing, SHA-256 and SmartScreen: What Each Proves | MalGuard Labs
text: A practical Windows guide to SHA-256 checksums, Authenticode signatures, Microsoft Defender SmartScreen reputation and the limits of each security signal. MalGuard Labs / Windows file trust Code signing is not the same as a safe download A checksum, a valid digital signature and a reputation warning answer different questions. Understanding the difference is more useful than treating any one signal as a green light. Published 20 October 2026 · Educational guidance, not a scan of a particular file Three independent questions Integrity, publisher identity and reputation Imagine finding two installers with identical names. One came from the developer's published release and one from an unknown mirror. The name alone cannot tell you whether their contents match. Even if a file was unchanged, it may still be unsafe for reasons that a checksum cannot detect. SHA-256: did the bytes match? A cryptographic hash is a fingerprint of the contents . If your locally calculated SHA-256 matches a trusted reference, this supports byte-for-byte integrity. It does not identify the author or tell you whether the software's behavior is safe. A checksum copied from the same untrusted mirror has limited independent value. Authenticode: who signed this artifact? Windows Authenticode can bind a software publisher's signing identity to a file and detect relevant changes after signing. A valid signature can help establish provenance and integrity relative to the signer. It does not mean Microsoft independently audited the application's code, or that its functions are harmless. SmartScreen: what does Windows know about reputation? Microsoft Defender SmartScreen considers file and publisher reputation. New, uncommon or unsigned programs may attract warnings; a warning is a reason for caution, not automatic proof of malware. Even newly signed software may need to build reputation. Verify without running the file Read the evidence before considering execution Start at the project's official release page and verify the exact artifact name and version. Windows includes PowerShell commands for viewing a file's SHA-256 hash and Authenticode status. Point these commands at a file you have already obtained from a trusted source; they inspect metadata without launching the installer. Check a checksum Get-FileHash -LiteralPath "C:\path\to\file.exe" -Algorithm SHA256 Compare the result against a SHA-256 published through an independently trusted channel. A mismatch is a reason to stop and investigate, never to ignore verification. Inspect a signature Get-AuthenticodeSignature -LiteralPath "C:\path\to\file.exe" Look at the reported signature status and signer information. An unsigned file has no Authenticode signer to verify. Do not disable Windows security protections merely to silence a warning. What does a trustworthy release note include? An honest release note distinguishes the exact version, source commit, checksum, signing status and platform-specific test evidence. It also states which tests were not performed. Unsigned previews must be identified as unsigned; a verified hash is not a replacement for publisher authentication. For MalGuard specifically, use the current release-status page and published evidence page for changing availability and limitations rather than inferring them from this general guide. Primary references Documentation worth checking Microsoft documents Get-FileHash , Get-AuthenticodeSignature and SmartScreen reputation . These sources describe Windows behavior; they are not an endorsement of MalGuard. Related: mod download checklist and how to read scan verdicts . More research guides Trust Center

title: Inside a Game Mod Archive: File Types, Structure and Warning Signs | MalGuard Labs
text: Learn how file extensions, file signatures, archive structure and parser limits affect game-mod safety checks, without executing unknown files. MalGuard Labs / Mod archive security Why a familiar ZIP file can still deserve scrutiny A mod archive is a container, not a promise. Its title, preview image and extension cannot certify every file inside it. Published 20 October 2026 · Educational guidance, not a scan of a particular file Understand the container Different evidence lives at different layers A ZIP or similar package can hold textures, configuration files, scripts, libraries and executables. The presence of a file type is not proof of malicious intent: many legitimate projects distribute functional code. The important questions are whether each component is expected, came from the right publisher and can be examined with adequate coverage. Extension versus actual file type A filename suffix is user-controlled text. Security tools may compare it with characteristic file bytes or internal structures, and flag disagreement for review. No single extension or magic-byte test is enough to certify file safety; OWASP recommends multiple independent validation layers. Unexpected contents Review the package's documented manifest and expected files. Unexplained executables, newly introduced scripts or renamed libraries merit additional questions. Conversely, a mod that legitimately needs a plugin file should not automatically be classified as malware simply for containing one. Incomplete inspection Nested archives, malformed data, password protection, unsupported formats or resource limits can leave an inspection incomplete. An analyzer should explicitly report what was skipped rather than silently treating missing coverage as a successful scan. A non-executing checklist Questions to answer before trusting an archive 01 Where is the original release? Find the developer's recognized project page and release notes. Treat unsolicited mirrors and anonymous re-uploads as unverified sources, even when they reproduce the original screenshots. 02 Does the package match documented contents? Compare the official version, manifest, file list and published checksum where provided. A matching checksum supports identity only when the reference comes from a trustworthy source. 03 Which parts could not be inspected? Look for explicit notes about inaccessible entries, unsupported formats and size limits. Incomplete coverage means the outcome remains uncertain, not safe. 04 Does the install request unusual actions? Stop when instructions unexpectedly ask you to disable built-in protection, run unexplained helper programs or reveal account credentials. Do not experiment with unknown files on your everyday device. Evidence over confidence What a scanner can honestly report Static inspection can analyze content without running it. That is valuable for reducing exposure, but it cannot establish all possible runtime behavior. Behavioral observation is a different kind of evidence and requires a properly justified, isolated environment. Do not assume a file was executed safely merely because a tool has a feature named “sandbox.” MalGuard's verdict guide explains why INCONCLUSIVE is meaningful and why no clean scan is a guarantee. This page documents general defensive reasoning, not test results for any specific mod. Further reading Reference and next steps OWASP's File Upload Cheat Sheet explains layered file validation, signature checks and resource-related risks. title: Fake Game Download Links: A Practical Guide to Website Trust Signals | MalGuard Labs
text: A defensive checklist for gaming download pages: impersonation, urgent prompts, domain names, redirects, account requests and why URL scanning has limits. MalGuard Labs / Gaming link safety How to question a game download link before clicking A convincing logo and a reassuring green icon are not evidence that a download page is authentic. The strongest checks begin with the original publisher. Published 20 October 2026 · Educational guidance, not a scan of a particular file Link and identity checks Ask whether the page belongs to who it claims Gaming communities often share mods, launchers, installers, maps and patches through many channels. A scam page may imitate a popular game site or developer while offering a different destination. You can evaluate warning signals without opening unknown downloads or entering personal details. The domain is the identity clue Check the full hostname against a known publisher address. Similar-looking spelling, extra subdomains and copied page branding can be misleading. A padlock or HTTPS connection secures transport to that hostname; it does not prove the site's operator is trustworthy. Urgency is a persuasion tactic “Download now or lose access,” “verify your account immediately,” and requests for unrelated payment details are reasons to pause. The FTC recommends reaching an organization through a trusted, independently found channel rather than responding to unexpected links. Redirects complicate inspection Shortened links and multiple redirects can obscure the final destination. A URL reputation tool might see only the starting page or an incomplete redirect chain. The absence of an alert is not evidence that every destination, download or future version is harmless. A safer decision path Five questions before using a gaming website 01 Can you find the publisher independently? Use the established project site or repository instead of a link forwarded by a stranger. Compare the domain, release notes and expected product name. 02 What information is the site asking for? A routine mod download should not unexpectedly require account recovery codes, unrelated passwords, or sensitive payment information. 03 Is a download being substituted? If the page suddenly offers an unrelated installer or an “update helper,” stop and confirm the original developer actually provides it. 04 What does the safety check cover? A URL scan might assess reputation or known indicators at a point in time; it does not automatically validate every file linked from a page or prove the operator's intentions. 05 Can you safely walk away? If identity or behavior remains uncertain, skip the download and return to a better-known source. Don't disable browser warnings just to make a link work. Sources and scope Separate educational guidance from a product verdict The US Federal Trade Commission's scam prevention guidance explains impersonation, urgency and independent contact verification. This article is general education, not an allegation about a particular gaming platform, and not a live investigation into any specific link. MalGuard publishes Game Scam Guard product information and trust limitations ; consult their current status rather than assuming this guide represents a completed scan or a guarantee. title: How to Contribute Safely to an Open-Source Security Project | MalGuard Labs
text: Learn how to choose a good first issue, use harmless synthetic tests, report vulnerabilities privately and write transparent pull requests. MalGuard Labs / Open-source engineering Your first security-project contribution does not need malware A clear bug report, reliable test or improved document can be a valuable security contribution. For a first PR, precision matters more than risk. Published 20 October 2026 · Educational guidance, not a scan of a particular file Choose a bounded contribution Start small enough that someone can review your work Open-source projects benefit from changes that others can understand, test and maintain. Begin by reading the README , license, CONTRIBUTING.md and security policy. Then look for good first issue tasks, such as clearer documentation, accessibility improvements, a broken link fix or an explanatory test using synthetic data. Documentation is engineering work If installation instructions assume a missing dependency or a test name is wrong, an accurate correction saves future contributors time. Check your commands on the stated platform and say when something was not tested. Make safe fixtures, not dangerous samples A synthetic fixture can exercise an extension mismatch, damaged archive structure or expected parser error without using real malware. Security tests should never require contributors to obtain or run a malicious sample on a normal computer. Keep the claim smaller than the evidence A passing unit test verifies a particular condition. It does not prove an entire product safe, that all platforms work, or that a code-signing provider has approved the release. List the exact commands and limitations in your PR description. Reviewable workflow Six steps to a useful pull request 01 Read and ask Study the issue, read related discussion and comment with the proposed scope before starting a larger change. 02 Work in a separate branch Use a fork or topic branch and change the smallest practical set of files. Avoid unrelated formatting changes. 03 Test without weakening protections Run applicable focused tests with harmless inputs. If a security gate fails, investigate it; do not silence it to obtain a green status. 04 State the evidence Describe the environment, commands, observed results and tests that were skipped. Redact sensitive logs and account details. 05 Submit and revise Open a PR with a clear summary, link the issue and respond to reviewer feedback. Review is collaboration, not a personal judgment. 06 Report vulnerabilities privately Potentially sensitive flaws belong in the project's private security channel when available. Public issues are for non-sensitive bugs and feature requests. Contribute to MalGuard Concrete places to begin MalGuard is an MIT-licensed defensive game-security project. Explore the contributor page , quickstart and beginner issues . The project prohibits real malware in development and CI; all proposed contributions require review. We do not promise acceptance, compensation or security certification. GitHub's contribution guide , private vulnerability reporting guidance and licensing documentation provide independent background. How to contribute More guides

title: امضای دیجیتال و هش SHA-256 در ویندوز؛ چه چیزی را ثابت می‌کنند؟ | MalGuard Labs
text: راهنمای فارسی بررسی SHA-256، امضای Authenticode و هشدارهای SmartScreen در ویندوز؛ همراه با محدودیت‌های هر روش و منابع رسمی. MalGuard Labs / آموزش فارسی · امنیت ویندوز امضای دیجیتال و هش فایل، یک چیز نیستند برای ارزیابی یک فایل دانلودشده، باید تفاوت «یکسان بودن محتوا»، «هویت امضاکننده» و «اعتبار نزد ویندوز» را بدانیم. هیچ‌کدام به‌تنهایی گواه امن بودن فایل نیستند. ۲۰ اکتبر ۲۰۲۶ · آموزش عمومی، نه نتیجهٔ اسکن یک فایل خاص سه مفهوم متفاوت از کجا بفهمیم یک فایل قابل اعتماد است؟ فرض کنید دو فایل نصب ویندوز نام یکسانی دارند. یکی از وب‌سایت رسمی سازنده دریافت شده و دیگری از یک سایت ناشناس. اسم یا آیکون یکسان هیچ تضمینی دربارهٔ محتوای واقعی آن‌ها نمی‌دهد. برای بررسی باید چند نشانهٔ مستقل را کنار هم گذاشت. هش SHA-256 هش، اثر انگشت محتوای فایل است. اگر هش فایل دانلودشده با هش اعلام‌شده در منبعی قابل اعتماد برابر باشد، می‌توان دربارهٔ یکسان بودن بایت‌های فایل نتیجه گرفت. اما اگر خود منبع هش جعلی باشد، یا فایل اصلی از ابتدا مشکل داشته باشد، این تطابق به معنی امن بودن نیست. امضای دیجیتال Authenticode امضای معتبر می‌تواند به بررسی هویت منتشرکننده و تمامیت فایل نسبت به امضای او کمک کند. بااین‌حال، امضاشدن یک برنامه به معنی بررسی کامل امنیت آن توسط مایکروسافت یا بی‌خطر بودن تمام رفتارهایش نیست. هشدار SmartScreen SmartScreen دربارهٔ شهرت فایل یا منتشرکننده از نشانه‌های مختلف استفاده می‌کند. برنامه‌های جدید یا ناشناخته ممکن است هشدار بگیرند. وجود هشدار الزاماً اثبات بدافزار بودن نیست؛ نبود هشدار هم گواه قطعی امن بودن نیست. بررسی بدون اجرای فایل دو دستور استاندارد ویندوز برای بررسی یک فایل مشخص که از منبع شناخته‌شده دریافت کرده‌اید، PowerShell ابزارهایی برای مشاهدهٔ هش و وضعیت امضا دارد. این دستورها خود فایل نصب را اجرا نمی‌کنند؛ فقط اطلاعات مربوط به آن را می‌خوانند. دیدن هش فایل Get-FileHash -LiteralPath "C:\path\to\file.exe" -Algorithm SHA256 هش به‌دست‌آمده را با مقدار اعلام‌شده از منبع معتبر مقایسه کنید. در صورت مغایرت، از اجرای فایل خودداری کنید و علت اختلاف را بررسی کنید. مشاهدهٔ وضعیت امضای فایل Get-AuthenticodeSignature -LiteralPath "C:\path\to\file.exe" وضعیت امضا و اطلاعات امضاکننده را بررسی کنید. اگر امضا وجود نداشت، نباید تصور کنید هش به‌تنهایی جای امضای معتبر را می‌گیرد. برای عبور از هشدارها، تنظیمات امنیتی ویندوز را غیرفعال نکنید. حدود اعتماد وقتی فایل برای یک بازی یا مود است، چه کنیم؟ صفحهٔ رسمی سازنده، شمارهٔ نسخه، هش منتشرشده، وضعیت امضا و توضیح آزمون‌ها را بررسی کنید. یک گزارش فنی معتبر باید مشخص کند چه چیزهایی آزمایش شده و چه چیزهایی هنوز بررسی نشده است. اگر فایل یا منبعش ناشناس است، ساده‌ترین تصمیم امن این است که سراغ آن نروید. برای وضعیت متغیر نسخه‌های MalGuard و GTA Guard به صفحهٔ انتشار رسمی و گزارش شواهد امنیتی مراجعه کنید. این مقاله گزارش تست یک فایل خاص نیست و تضمین امنیت ارائه نمی‌کند. منابع اصلی مستندات مایکروسافت توضیحات رسمی دربارهٔ Get-FileHash ، Get-AuthenticodeSignature و اعتبار SmartScreen را مطالعه کنید. این منابع رفتار ویندوز را توضیح می‌دهند و تأییدیه‌ای برای MalGuard محسوب نمی‌شوند. بیشتر بخوانید: آموزش فارسی امنیت مادهای GTA و نسخهٔ انگلیسی این راهنما . بازگشت به بخش تحقیقات
